title: Choosing Kind Words During Disagreement
paragraphs: During a heated discussion about splitting household chores, Ridwan feels tempted to bring up an old, unrelated complaint just to win the argument against his roommate more decisively.
He catches himself before saying it, recognizing that dragging up the past would only hurt his roommate unnecessarily and turn a simple disagreement into something far more painful for both of them.
Instead, he sticks to the actual topic, calmly explaining his side without insults or exaggeration, even though staying focused feels harder than simply letting his frustration spill out freely.

By the end of the conversation, they reach a fair compromise about the chores, and Ridwan feels relieved that he chose restraint over a cheap victory that would have cost their friendship something real.
